$comment: design §6.2 (S6), §6.4, §7.5; plan WP-11; lead decisions D11 (D-20261111-f3d39c: the consequence classes are owned here), D12 (D-20261111-f174ea: a judgment is keyed per candidate, unit and seat; the first call of a candidate judges its requirements, class, matching units and ledger relations and every unit, a later reference point's call only the units whose key is new), D14 (D-20261111-1aa1b3: two judgments and a one-line reason for every unit, a quote only where the situation or the action matches). Every unit, quote and ledger entry is named by the packet's own label (n, q, e); code turns labels back into stored ids, checks that every unit is judged once, that a quote is a span of its unit and is present exactly where a match is yes, and that every matching unit has its following and contribution (stage_judge.answer_problems). This schema holds the shape.
title: S6 judgment

requirements.$comment: D-20261020-71699d: the eight admission requirements, each judged met, unmet or uncertain with its reason (§6.4 admission)

consequence_class.$comment: D11: the one owner of the consequence classes (§7.5's six); tables/unit_outcome.json's promotion row and the ranking read this enum

no_longer_arises.$comment: §6.4 obsolete: evidence that the situation no longer arises, which a lifecycle candidate needs; false with no evidence otherwise

unit_judgment.$comment: §6.2 per unit: situation match, action match, a one-line reason, and (D14) a quote of the unit only where either match is yes, empty otherwise

matching_unit.$comment: §6.2 per candidate, for each matching unit: its following and its contribution to the outcome, each with evidence ids, kept apart from the event's consequence

ledger_relation.$comment: §6.2: the relation to each retrieved ledger entry
